$comment: AUTHORITY for the time a Semiont client keeps: every wait it makes, every interval it measures and every jitter it draws follows a clock and a random source its caller controls, so a caller who moves the clock sees each wait end when this table says, and not a millisecond before. How a caller controls them is each ecosystem's own: the runtime's test clock where the runtime owns time (Go's testing/synctest, Tokio's paused clock, the running asyncio loop's clock, a JavaScript test runner's fake timers), and public parameters of the standard types where the ecosystem's waits take them (Kotlin a CoroutineContext, a TimeSource and a Random; Swift a Clock and a RandomNumberGenerator; C# a TimeProvider and a Random); protocol/specs/src/client/surface.json's `clock` section names each SDK's. What is outside it: a reading of the wall clock, which compares now with an instant a server stated (a token's `exp`) or stamps a record, reads the platform's wall clock, which moving the caller's clock need not move; and the randomness of a secret (a PKCE verifier, a nonce, a client assertion's `jti`), which stays the platform's cryptographic source. Every SDK runs these cases in its own process, on its own controlled clock, at the timings protocol/specs/src/client/timing.json states, never overridden: moving a clock an hour costs nothing. The conformance drivers, which are other processes on real time, do not run them. Every jitter a case draws is the lowest its source can give, so the equal jitter of a step is half the step. A case names its `subject`, which says what the runner builds and what it counts, and what it is (`case`); `given` states what a subject leaves open. Every network a subject speaks over is faked in the runner's process, and answers at once unless the subject says otherwise. Subjects: `refusedStream`: a transport whose gateway refuses every subscribe with 503, with a `Retry-After` of `given.retryAfterSeconds` when stated; it counts subscribe requests. `unansweredStream`: a transport whose gateway never answers a subscribe; it counts subscribe requests. `degradedStream`: as `refusedStream`; it counts the times the transport's state has become `degraded`. `scopeTaken`: a transport whose gateway answers every subscribe with a stream it holds open, carrying no resource's scope; `act` takes a resource's scope; it counts subscribe requests. `scopeLetGo`: as `scopeTaken`, taking a resource's scope once its stream is open, as the case begins; `act` lets it go; it counts subscribe requests. `handoffLinger`: as `scopeTaken`; it counts the connections the client has closed. `renewal`: a session signed in on an access token issued now, by the wall clock, that lives `given.lifetimeSeconds`, whose issuer renews it every time with a token that lives as long, issued when it renews, and whose gateway accepts every token; it counts renewals. `deviceGrant`: a sign-in by the device grant whose issuer answers the device authorization with a code that lives 900 seconds and an `interval` of `given.intervalSeconds` (none when absent), and answers each ask of its token endpoint with the next of `given.answers`, as an `error` beside a 400, the last repeating; it counts asks of the token endpoint. `heldJobStall`: a worker's claims, over a transport that answers `job:claim` with one job, claimed at the case's start; the job reports nothing but what `act` reports, a progress report of that job; it counts the stalls the claims' `stalled` says. `discovery`: `subscribeDiscovery` given `discoveryIntervalMs` as its interval, over a discovery transport that answers its first read with one managed knowledge base and every read after it as unchanged, whose changes are read as they come; it counts reads. `invalidationWindow`: a client observing the `events` query of one resource (protocol/specs/src/client/refresh.json), whose every `browse:events-requested` is answered; `act` delivers from the wire a `mark:added` frame of that resource, which refetches the key; it counts `browse:events-requested` requests sent. `saveDebounce`: a cache that keeps its values, through a storage that records each save; `act` sets a value; it counts saves. `jobFollower`: a client's `mark.delegate`, whose follower keeps no stall deadline, over a transport that answers `job:create` with a job and every `job:status-requested` with that job `running`; the job says nothing but what `act` delivers from the wire, a progress report of that job; it counts `job:status-requested` requests sent. `unansweredRequest`: the gateway's health check (`healthCheck`), over a network that never answers it; it counts the times it has failed as unanswered. `unansweredEmit`: one emit, over a network that never answers `POST /bus/emit`; it counts the emit's attempts. The subject is built, and set going, as the case begins. `steps` run in order: `"settle"` lets what is ready run, and what that makes ready, until nothing more is, and moves no time; `pass` settles, then moves the clock, letting what falls due run as it does; `"act"` does the subject's action, then settles; `counted` states how many times what the subject counts has happened since the case began, once what is ready has run. A duration is milliseconds, or `{"timing": <a name of protocol/specs/src/client/timing.json>}` with `times` and `plusMs` to scale and move it, the name of a retry budget followed by `.` and one of its members (`emitRetry.initialDelayMs`). A case states each wait's end as a pair: nothing at a millisecond before it, and the thing counted at it.

notYetReached.typescript: The seven AbortSignal.timeout deadlines become timers the SDK sets, and a runner under vitest's fake timers with Math.random giving its lowest.
notYetReached.rust: A random source the caller gives replaces the UUID draw behind the jitter, and a runner on a paused runtime over a faked network.
notYetReached.go: A *rand.Rand the caller gives replaces the global draw behind the jitter, and a runner in a synctest bubble over an in-memory network.
notYetReached.kotlin: The context, clock and random source become public on every maker that waits, the System.nanoTime readings and the JDK's request timeouts go, and a runner under runTest.
notYetReached.csharp: The stream's reconnect draws equal jitter from the transport's Random, the redirect sign-in and the session factory hand on the caller's clock and Random, and a runner on a FakeTimeProvider.

cases.subject: refusedStream
cases.case: a stream the gateway refuses is opened again after half of reconnectMs, then after half of twice it: the backoff doubles

cases.subject: refusedStream
cases.case: the backoff stops doubling at maxReconnectMs

cases.subject: refusedStream
cases.case: a refusal's Retry-After is a floor on the wait before the stream is opened again

cases.subject: unansweredStream
cases.case: a subscribe the gateway never answers has failed at streamOpenTimeoutMs, and the stream is opened again on the backoff

cases.subject: degradedStream
cases.case: a stream that has been reconnecting for degradedThresholdMs is degraded

cases.subject: scopeTaken
cases.case: a scope taken is carried by a new stream once reconnectDebounceMs has passed

cases.subject: scopeLetGo
cases.case: a scope let go is dropped by a new stream once lazyRemoveMs has passed

cases.subject: handoffLinger
cases.case: the stream a handoff superseded is read for lingerMs after its successor opens, and closed then

cases.subject: renewal
cases.case: a token that lives fifteen seconds is renewed after minRefreshDelayMs, the floor, and so is each one after it

cases.subject: renewal
cases.case: a token that lives an hour is renewed refreshBeforeExpMs before it expires, and not two seconds sooner: its claims are whole seconds, so it may have been issued up to a second before now, and the wall clock its expiry is read against moves on while the case runs

cases.subject: deviceGrant
cases.case: an issuer that states no interval is asked every devicePollMs, the first time too

cases.subject: deviceGrant
cases.case: an issuer that states an interval of none is asked no oftener than devicePollFloorMs

cases.subject: deviceGrant
cases.case: slow_down lengthens the wait by deviceSlowDownMs, for every ask after it

cases.subject: heldJobStall
cases.case: a held job is said to have stalled at the first check at which its silence is longer than heldJobStallMs, and only once

cases.subject: heldJobStall
cases.case: a progress report starts the held job's silence again

cases.subject: discovery
cases.case: the discovery document is read at once, and again after each interval

cases.subject: invalidationWindow
cases.case: the first invalidation of a key refetches at once, those inside its window refetch once when it closes, and one after the window at once

cases.subject: saveDebounce
cases.case: a cache saves its values saveDebounceMs after they changed

cases.subject: saveDebounce
cases.case: the wait before a save starts again at each change, so a burst of changes is one save

cases.subject: jobFollower
cases.case: a followed job silent for jobSilenceMs is asked for its status, then every jobStatusPollMs, and a frame of it starts the silence again

cases.subject: unansweredRequest
cases.case: a request the gateway never answers fails at httpRequestTimeoutMs, and is not made again

cases.subject: unansweredEmit
cases.case: each attempt of an emit the gateway never answers ends at emitTimeoutMs, and the next is made on emitRetry's backoff, which doubles
